methodology.description: Public draft-helper PPR redraft board. Player value and market cost are intentionally kept separate. Rankings blend broad expert consensus, current projections, recent independent expert boards and material preseason/news context; ADP is treated as price rather than player quality. League scoring, roster construction, draft slot, drafted players, positional scarcity and next-pick pressure are applied by the client recommendation engine.
rankingInputs: FantasyPros 2026 PPR consensus, injury feed and current market data checked Sept. 2
ESPN Aug. 31 running-back tiers and current fantasy news checked Sept. 2
RotoWire Sept. 2 PPR rankings, health reports and ADP
CBS Sports Sept. 2 PPR consensus and analyst boards
Rotoworld/NBC Sports late-preseason rankings and player-news context checked through Sept. 2
Yahoo Sports, Fantasy Life and other independent market sources checked through Sept. 2
methodology.marketInput: Current PPR ADP remains a separate market-price input, cross-checked across RotoWire, FantasyPros, Sleeper-market samples, CBS/Yahoo and other platform references. ADP is not used as a substitute for player value; large gaps remain when injury, availability, role uncertainty or expert disagreement justifies them.
newsInputs: Amon-Ra St. Brown moves from No. 7 to No. 6. RotoWire's Sept. 2 PPR board ranks him sixth and CBS' fresh PPR consensus also places him sixth, creating a clearer cross-source center than the prior file reflected.

Jonathan Taylor moves from No. 8 to No. 7. CBS' Sept. 2 PPR consensus has him seventh and several CBS analysts place him as high as third overall; RotoWire remains more conservative at No. 10, so the disagreement range stays wide.

Christian McCaffrey moves from No. 6 to No. 8. RotoWire has him seventh and CBS consensus eighth, while ESPN's Aug. 31 RB tiers remain notably cautious because of last season's 413-touch workload. His ceiling is still first-round caliber, but the cross-source center no longer supports No. 6.

Ja'Marr Chase remains No. 3. Cincinnati plans to limit him in practice after the recent knee hyperextension, but coach Zac Taylor said he feels good about Chase's progress and current reports still point toward Week 1 availability.

Ashton Jeanty remains No. 23, but confidence improves slightly. Raiders GM John Spytek said Sept. 1 that Jeanty is in a good spot and could return sooner than expected; he avoided injured reserve but had not yet returned to practice, so Week 1 remains uncertain.

Josh Jacobs remains sharply discounted while on the Commissioner's Exempt List. MarShawn Lloyd remains the preferred Green Bay backfield value while Jacobs is unavailable; no firm Jacobs return date has emerged.
methodology.notes: Expert disagreement is preserved with expertHigh/expertLow ranges; unresolved injuries, discipline risk and genuine model disagreement can intentionally widen those ranges. Confidence reflects agreement plus news certainty, not ceiling. This file is used only by smhillis/sleeper-draft-helper-public and must not be copied into or used to modify Scott's personal Sleeper Draft Assistant.

players.name: Christian McCaffrey

players.name: MarShawn Lloyd
players.news: Added after Josh Jacobs was placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Lloyd is the projected starter entering Week 1 and Fantasy Life moved him into the top 65, while older rankings remain far lower. Market ADP has been rising quickly, so the board keeps a wide uncertainty band instead of pricing the new role as settled fact.

players.name: Josh Jacobs
players.news: Major downgrade remains in force. Jacobs is on the Commissioner's Exempt List and cannot practice or play while listed, with no firm return date. Trailing ADP remains stale relative to the availability risk, so market price is intentionally not treated as player value.
